overview: The committee hosted a presentation on forming a local Mothers Out Front chapter and reviewed 2023 priorities, including building electrification and tree canopy preservation. Members also discussed upcoming community events and received updates on city staffing and park renovation projects.

items.title: Mothers Out Front Presentation
items.summary: Christina Elaine introduced the nascent Medford chapter of Mothers Out Front, focusing on grassroots climate action and composting awareness through events like the Pumpkin Smash.

items.title: Minutes Approval
items.summary: Approved the minutes of the April 12 meeting as amended.

items.title: Membership and Administrative Updates
items.summary: Discussed the appointment of new members and the potential to expand the committee to 15 members to increase volunteer capacity.

items.title: Rain Barrel Distribution and Meeting Logistics
items.summary: Staff reported that over 200 rain barrels were sold for the upcoming distribution event, and the committee discussed holding an in-person meeting this summer.

items.title: Departmental Staffing and Capital Projects
items.summary: Alicia Hunt updated the committee on multiple staff vacancies being filled and ongoing park renovations at Morrison and Gillis Parks and the Clipper Ship Connector.

items.title: Report on Meeting with the Mayor
items.summary: Lauretta James reported that Mayor Lungo-Koehn supports the committee's priorities, including electrification, increasing the tree canopy, and implementing integrated pest management to reduce rodenticide use.

items.title: Harvest Your Energy Festival Planning
items.summary: Discussed strategies to expand the festival, including a potential beer garden on city property and increased participation from environmental artists.

items.title: 2023 Committee Priorities
items.summary: Reviewed a priority list encompassing building and transportation electrification, heat pump promotion, and tree equity.

items.title: Circle the Square Preparation
items.summary: Planned staffing and educational displays, such as invasive plant samples and native seeds, for the June 17 community event.

items.title: State Reforestation Legislation and Tree Ordinance
items.summary: Lauretta James highlighted an upcoming legislative briefing for a state municipal reforestation bill and discussed the need for a certified arborist to support a local tree ordinance.

items.title: Regional Green Building Guidelines
items.summary: Alicia Hunt updated the committee on draft guidelines for energy-efficient development created through a regional partnership with Malden and Melrose.
